Hi Evelyn,

We're updating our vendor risk file ahead of an internal audit and need a few items from Redwood to complete Finovate's review:

- Full current subprocessor list (names, roles, countries, and activation dates)
- Data transfer mechanisms used for EU->US processing (SCCs, adequacy, or other safeguards)
- Confirmation of whether any subprocessors have access to plaintext customer data and what controls are in place (encryption at rest/in transit, KMS, HSM)
- Dates of last SOC 2 and external penetration test reports (we don't need the full reports yet, just timestamps and contact to request evidence)

Could you also confirm if Redwood offers on-prem or VPC-deployed options for customers in regulated payments? If there's a standard subprocessor matrix export you can share, that would be ideal.

We have an upcoming compliance checkpoint on Apr 20; if possible we'd like materials by Apr 13.

Lee — quick technical notes to complement Evelyn's reply:

- Subprocessors: we categorize by role (inference compute, logging/metrics, storage/backups, observability). The matrix will include role, provider name, country, and "access scope" (e.g., tokenized metadata only vs. KV cache access).
- For hosted customers we use encrypted at rest (AES-256) + TLS1.3 in transit. Keys are managed by Redwood by default; enterprise customers can provide a customer-managed KMS (AWS KMS, GCP Cloud KMS, Azure Key Vault).
- SCCs are in place for EU->US. We also offer an export path for customers requiring a private deployment (no cross-border transfers) and can support on-prem for large regulated payments customers.
- SOC 2 Type II most recent reporting period ended 2025-11-30. External pentest: completed 2026-02-15. We will supply redacted evidence and a contact from our security team to request full artifacts under an NDA if needed.

If you'd like a brief tech call, I can join Monday as well.

-Rishi
Head of Solutions, Redwood Dedicated
